newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: BP says sees $600 mln investment in Colombo in '97.
newsitem.headline: BP says sees $600 mln investment in Colombo in '97.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc's Colombian subsidiary will be looking to invest a net sum of about $600 million in Colombia in 1997, its executive director John Doust said on Thursday.
The figure will match net investments for 1996 which took BP's total investments in Colombia to $2 billion, Doust said.

He said one of the major challenges next year would be to iron out difficulties with the contract on the giant Piedemonte field in Colombia's eastern plains but predicted the field, still at the test stage, would come on stream by the end of 1999.
Investment in the Piedemonte could total more than $2.2 billion, though part of that would be put up by state oil company Ecopetrol, Doust said.

The second phase of the Cupiagua and Cusiana fields is set to be complete by the end of next year, marking an overall investment of $4 billion to be shared between BP and its associates, Ecopetrol, Triton and Total.
Doust said the fields should be producing 500,000 barrels a day by the end of 1997, up from current levels of about 175,000 barrels a day.
